newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt opens gas field off northern coast.
newsitem.headline: Egypt opens gas field off northern coast.

text.p: Egyptian Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi has inaugurated a natural gas field off the Mediterranean city of Port Said, the ministry said on Saturday.

The Waqar field, operated by the Egyptian-Italian firm Petrobel (Belayim Petroleum), has a daily production capacity of 42 million cubic feet (1.2 million cubic metres) of gas and 2,700 barrel of condensates from two wells.
The development project includes installing a remote-controlled rig and building three pipelines to link the Waqar and nearby Port Fouad fields, the ministry said in a statement.
It said $39.5 million was invested in the project, 55 km (34 miles) off the coast, during the past 11 months.
Banbi opened the field earlier this week during a tour with visiting Yemeni Oil Minister Mohammad Said al-Attar, a ministry official told Reuters.
The field was discovered in 1995 and developed last year, he added.
Petrobel is a joint venture between the Egyptian government firm Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation and Italy's Agip SpA.
The government is switching to natural gas from oil for generating electricity in Egypt, freeing larger volumes of crude oil for export.
